title: Shift-Family Headcount
description:
## Task

Two words belong to the same shift family when they have the same length and one turns into the other by moving every letter the same number of steps forward in the alphabet, wrapping from `z` back to `a`. For example `abc` becomes `bcd` after one step and `zab` after 25 steps. Count how many different families the list contains. A family needs only one word to exist, and repeated words belong to the same family.

## Input

- `words` — a list of non-empty lowercase words. It may be empty.

## Output

The number of distinct shift families.

## Example

```python
shift_family_count(["abc", "bcd", "az", "ba", "xyz"])  # returns 2
shift_family_count(["a", "b"])  # returns 1
shift_family_count([])  # returns 0
```

## Constraints

- 0 ≤ number of words ≤ 10^5
- 1 ≤ length of each word ≤ 30
- Words contain only the lowercase letters `a`-`z`.
- Comparing every pair of words is too slow for the largest inputs.
